title: JEE Main 2023 · 24 Jan · Shift 2 (recreated)

qs.stem: The number of real solutions of the equation 3(x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup>) − 2(x + 1/x) + 5 = 0 is
steps: Let t = x + 1/x, so x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> = t<sup>2</sup> − 2.
3t<sup>2</sup> − 2t − 1 = 0 gives t = 1 or t = −1/3.
For real x, |t| ≥ 2, so neither value is possible: no real solutions.

qs.stem: The value of ((1 + sin(2π/9) + i cos(2π/9)) / (1 + sin(2π/9) − i cos(2π/9)))<sup>3</sup> is
steps: Write sin(2π/9) = cos β and cos(2π/9) = sin β with β = π/2 − 2π/9.
The ratio is (1 + e<sup>iβ</sup>)/(1 + e<sup>−iβ</sup>) = e<sup>iβ</sup>.
Cube: e<sup>3iβ</sup> = e<sup>i5π/6</sup> = −√3/2 + i/2 = −(1/2)(√3 − i).

qs.stem: The number of integers greater than 7000 that can be formed using the digits 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 without repetition is
steps: Five-digit numbers: 5! = 120.
Four-digit numbers greater than 7000 start with 7 or 8: 2 × 4 × 3 × 2 = 48.

qs.stem: If (<sup>30</sup>C<sub>1</sub>)<sup>2</sup> + 2(<sup>30</sup>C<sub>2</sub>)<sup>2</sup> + 3(<sup>30</sup>C<sub>3</sub>)<sup>2</sup> + … + 30(<sup>30</sup>C<sub>30</sub>)<sup>2</sup> = α · 60!/(30!)<sup>2</sup>, then α is equal to
steps: Use k·<sup>n</sup>C<sub>k</sub> = n·<sup>n−1</sup>C<sub>k−1</sub>, so the sum is 30 · Σ<sup>30</sup>C<sub>k</sub> · <sup>29</sup>C<sub>k−1</sub> = 30 · <sup>59</sup>C<sub>29</sub>.
α = 30 · 30/60 = 15.

qs.stem: The locus of the midpoints of the chords of the circle C<sub>1</sub>: (x − 4)<sup>2</sup> + (y − 5)<sup>2</sup> = 4 which subtend an angle θ<sub>i</sub> at the centre of the circle C<sub>1</sub> is a circle of radius r<sub>i</sub>. If θ<sub>1</sub> = π/3, θ<sub>3</sub> = 2π/3 and r<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> = r<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup> + r<sub>3</sub><sup>2</sup>, then θ<sub>2</sub> is equal to
steps: The midpoint of a chord subtending θ at the centre is at distance 2 cos(θ/2) from it, so r = 2 cos(θ/2).
r<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> = 4 cos<sup>2</sup>(π/6) = 3 and r<sub>3</sub><sup>2</sup> = 4 cos<sup>2</sup>(π/3) = 1, so r<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup> = 2.
4 cos<sup>2</sup>(θ<sub>2</sub>/2) = 2 gives θ<sub>2</sub> = π/2.

qs.stem: The equations of the sides AB and AC of a triangle ABC are (λ + 1)x + λy = 4 and λx + (1 − λ)y + λ = 0 respectively. Its vertex A is on the y-axis and its orthocentre is (1, 2). The length of the tangent from the point C to the part of the parabola y<sup>2</sup> = 6x in the first quadrant is
steps: A on the y-axis: 4/λ = λ/(λ − 1) gives λ = 2, so AB: 3x + 2y = 4, AC: 2x − y + 2 = 0 and A = (0, 2).
AH is horizontal, so BC is vertical, x = k. CH ⊥ AB gives k = −1/2 and C = (−1/2, 1).
The tangent from C touching the parabola in the first quadrant touches at (3/2, 3); the length is √(4 + 4) = 2√2.

qs.stem: The set of values of a for which lim<sub>x→a</sub> ([x − 5] − [2x + 2]) = 0, where [ζ] denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to ζ, is equal to
steps: [x − 5] − [2x + 2] = [x] − [2x] − 7.
On [−7.5, −6.5) the value of [x] − [2x] is 7, so the expression is 0.
At a = −7.5 the left limit is 1 and at a = −6.5 the right limit is −1, so those two points fail: (−7.5, −6.5).

qs.stem: Let p and q be two statements. Then ~(p ∧ (p → ~q)) is equivalent to
steps: p → ~q is ~p ∨ ~q.
p ∧ (~p ∨ ~q) = p ∧ ~q.
Its negation is ~p ∨ q.

qs.stem: Let the six numbers a<sub>1</sub>, a<sub>2</sub>, …, a<sub>6</sub> be in A.P. and a<sub>1</sub> + a<sub>3</sub> = 10. If the mean of these six numbers is 19/2 and their variance is σ<sup>2</sup>, then 8σ<sup>2</sup> is equal to
steps: a<sub>1</sub> + a<sub>3</sub> = 2a + 2d = 10 and the mean a + 5d/2 = 19/2 give d = 3 and a = 2.
The numbers 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 have variance d<sup>2</sup>(n<sup>2</sup> − 1)/12 = 9 × 35/12 = 105/4.
8σ<sup>2</sup> = 210.

qs.stem: The number of square matrices of order 5 with entries from the set {0, 1}, such that the sum of all the elements in each row is 1 and the sum of all the elements in each column is also 1, is
steps: Each row and each column has exactly one 1, so the matrix is a permutation matrix.
There are 5! = 120 of them.

qs.stem: Let A be a 3 × 3 matrix such that |adj(adj(adj A))| = 12<sup>4</sup>. Then |A<sup>−1</sup> adj A| is equal to
steps: For a 3 × 3 matrix |adj A| = |A|<sup>2</sup>, so |adj(adj(adj A))| = |A|<sup>8</sup> = 12<sup>4</sup> and |A|<sup>2</sup> = 12.
|A<sup>−1</sup> adj A| = |A|<sup>−1</sup> · |A|<sup>2</sup> = |A| = 2√3.

qs.stem: If the system of equations x + 2y + 3z = 3, 4x + 3y − 4z = 4 and 8x + 4y − λz = 9 + μ has infinitely many solutions, then the ordered pair (λ, μ) is equal to
steps: Infinitely many solutions need the determinant to vanish: 5λ − 72 = 0, so λ = 72/5.
Row 3 = a(Row 1) + b(Row 2) with a = −8/5, b = 12/5.
Then 9 + μ = 3a + 4b = 24/5, so μ = −21/5.

qs.stem: If f(x) = 2<sup>2x</sup> / (2<sup>2x</sup> + 2), x ∈ R, then f(1/2023) + f(2/2023) + f(3/2023) + … + f(2022/2023) is equal to
steps: f(x) + f(1 − x) = 4<sup>x</sup>/(4<sup>x</sup> + 2) + 2/(4<sup>x</sup> + 2) = 1.
The 2022 terms form 1011 such pairs, so the sum is 1011.

qs.stem: Let f(x) be a function such that f(x + y) = f(x) · f(y) for all x, y ∈ N. If f(1) = 3 and Σ<sub>k=1</sub><sup>n</sup> f(k) = 3279, then the value of n is
steps: f(k) = 3<sup>k</sup>.
3(3<sup>n</sup> − 1)/2 = 3279 gives 3<sup>n</sup> = 2187 = 3<sup>7</sup>, so n = 7.

qs.stem: If f(x) = x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup>f′(1) + xf″(2) − f″′(3), x ∈ R, then
steps: Let f′(1) = a and f″(2) = b. Then f′ = 3x<sup>2</sup> − 2ax + b, f″ = 6x − 2a, f″′ = 6.
f′(1) = a gives b = 3a − 3; f″(2) = b gives 12 − 2a = b; so a = 3, b = 6.
f(x) = x<sup>3</sup> − 3x<sup>2</sup> + 6x − 6: f(0) = −6, f(1) = −2, f(2) = 2, f(3) = 12. Only 2f(0) − f(1) + f(3) = f(2) holds.

qs.stem: ∫<sub>3/4</sub><sup>3√2/4</sup> 48 / √(9 − 4x<sup>2</sup>) dx is equal to
steps: ∫ dx/√(9 − 4x<sup>2</sup>) = (1/2) sin<sup>−1</sup>(2x/3).
48 × (1/2) = 24, with 2x/3 running from 1/2 to √2/2.

qs.stem: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (x<sup>2</sup> − 3y<sup>2</sup>)dx + 3xy dy = 0, y(1) = 1. Then 6y<sup>2</sup>(e) is equal to
steps: Homogeneous: put y = vx, so x dv/dx = −1/(3v) and 3v dv = −dx/x.
(3/2)v<sup>2</sup> = −ln x + 3/2, so y<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup>(1 − (2/3) ln x).
At x = e: y<sup>2</sup> = e<sup>2</sup>/3, so 6y<sup>2</sup> = 2e<sup>2</sup>.

qs.stem: Let α = 4i + 3j + 5k and β = i + 2j − 4k. Let β1 be parallel to α and β2 be perpendicular to α. If β = β1 + β2, then the value of 5β2 · (i + j + k) is
steps: β1 = (α·β/|α|2)α = (−10/50)α = −α/5.
β2 = β − β1 = (9/5, 13/5, −3).

qs.stem: Let the plane containing the line of intersection of the planes P<sub>1</sub>: x + (λ + 4)y + z = 1 and P<sub>2</sub>: 2x + y + z = 2 pass through the points (0, 1, 0) and (1, 0, 1). Then the distance of the point (2λ, λ, −λ) from the plane P<sub>2</sub> is
steps: The plane is (x + (λ + 4)y + z − 1) + μ(2x + y + z − 2) = 0. Through (1, 0, 1): 1 + μ = 0, so μ = −1.
Through (0, 1, 0): (λ + 3) − μ = 0 gives λ = −4.
The point is (−8, −4, 4); its distance from 2x + y + z − 2 = 0 is |−16 − 4 + 4 − 2|/√6 = 18/√6 = 3√6.

qs.stem: If the foot of the perpendicular drawn from (1, 9, 7) to the line passing through the point (3, 2, 1) and parallel to the planes x + 2y + z = 0 and 3y − z = 3 is (α, β, γ), then α + β + γ is equal to
steps: The line direction is the cross product of the normals (1, 2, 1) and (0, 3, −1): (−5, 1, 3).
Points on the line: (3 − 5s, 2 + s, 1 + 3s). The vector from (1, 9, 7) is perpendicular to the direction when 35s − 35 = 0, so s = 1.
Foot = (−2, 3, 4), sum = 5.

qs.stem: If (1<sup>3</sup> + 2<sup>3</sup> + 3<sup>3</sup> + … up to n terms) / (1·3 + 2·5 + 3·7 + … up to n terms) = 9/5, then the value of n is
steps: Numerator = [n(n + 1)/2]<sup>2</sup>. Denominator = Σk(2k + 1) = n(n + 1)(4n + 5)/6.
Ratio = 3n(n + 1)/(2(4n + 5)) = 9/5, so 5n<sup>2</sup> − 19n − 30 = 0.

qs.stem: Let the sum of the coefficients of the first three terms in the expansion of (x − 3/x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>n</sup>, x ≠ 0, n ∈ N, be 376. Then the coefficient of x<sup>4</sup> is equal to
steps: The first three coefficients are 1, −3n and 9n(n − 1)/2. Their sum 376 gives 3n<sup>2</sup> − 5n − 250 = 0, so n = 10.
General term: <sup>10</sup>C<sub>r</sub>(−3)<sup>r</sup> x<sup>10 − 3r</sup>; x<sup>4</sup> needs r = 2.
Coefficient = 45 × 9 = 405.

qs.stem: Let S = {θ ∈ [0, 2π) : tan(π cos θ) + tan(π sin θ) = 0}. Then Σ<sub>θ∈S</sub> sin<sup>2</sup>(θ + π/4) is equal to
steps: tan(π cos θ) = tan(−π sin θ) gives cos θ + sin θ = k, an integer, so √2 sin(θ + π/4) = k with k = 0, ±1.
k = 0 gives θ = 3π/4, 7π/4 where sin<sup>2</sup>(θ + π/4) = 0.
k = ±1 gives θ = 0, π/2, π, 3π/2, each with sin<sup>2</sup> = 1/2. Sum = 4 × 1/2 = 2.

qs.stem: The equations of the sides AB, BC and CA of a triangle ABC are 2x + y = 0, x + py = 21a (a ≠ 0) and x − y = 3 respectively. Let P(2, a) be the centroid of the triangle ABC. Then (BC)<sup>2</sup> is equal to
steps: A = AB ∩ CA = (1, −2). Take B = (b, −2b) and C = (c, c − 3).
Centroid (2, a): b + c = 5 and c − 2b − 5 = 3a, which give a = −b. B on BC gives p = 11; C on BC then gives b = −3, c = 8, a = 3.

qs.stem: The minimum number of elements that must be added to the relation R = {(a, b), (b, c), (b, d)} on the set {a, b, c, d} so that it is an equivalence relation is
steps: An equivalence relation containing (a, b), (b, c), (b, d) makes a, b, c, d one class, so it is all 16 ordered pairs.
R already has 3, so 16 − 3 = 13 must be added.

qs.stem: Let f be a differentiable function defined on [0, π/2] such that f(x) > 0 and f(x) + ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> f(t)√(1 − (log<sub>e</sub> f(t))<sup>2</sup>) dt = e, ∀ x ∈ [0, π/2]. Then (6 log<sub>e</sub> f(π/6))<sup>2</sup> is equal to
steps: Differentiate: f′ + f√(1 − (ln f)<sup>2</sup>) = 0. With u = ln f: u′ = −√(1 − u<sup>2</sup>).
sin<sup>−1</sup>u = −x + C and f(0) = e (u = 1) gives C = π/2, so u = cos x and f = e<sup>cos x</sup>.
ln f(π/6) = √3/2, so (6 × √3/2)<sup>2</sup> = 27.

qs.stem: If the area of the region bounded by the curves y<sup>2</sup> − 2y = −x and x + y = 0 is A, then 8A is equal to
steps: The curves are x = 2y − y<sup>2</sup> and x = −y; they meet where 2y − y<sup>2</sup> = −y, so y = 0 and y = 3.
A = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>3</sup> (3y − y<sup>2</sup>) dy = 27/2 − 9 = 9/2.

qs.stem: The urns A, B and C contain 4 red, 6 black; 5 red, 5 black and λ red, 4 black balls respectively. One of the urns is selected at random and a ball is drawn. If the ball drawn is red and the probability that it is drawn from urn C is 0.4, then the square of the length of the side of the largest equilateral triangle inscribed in the parabola y<sup>2</sup> = λx with one vertex at the vertex of the parabola is
steps: Let r = λ/(λ + 4). Bayes: r/(0.4 + 0.5 + r) = 0.4, so r = 0.6 and λ = 6.
In y<sup>2</sup> = 6x, an equilateral triangle with a vertex at the origin has its other vertices at y = ±x tan 30°: (x/√3)<sup>2</sup> = 6x gives x = 18, y = 6√3.

qs.stem: If two vectors P = î + 2mĵ + mk̂ and Q = 4î − 2ĵ + mk̂ are perpendicular to each other, then the value of m will be
steps: Perpendicular vectors have P·Q = 0.
4 − 4m + m<sup>2</sup> = 0, so (m − 2)<sup>2</sup> = 0 and m = 2.

qs.stem: The frequency (ν) of an oscillating liquid drop may depend upon the radius (r) of the drop, the density (ρ) of the liquid and the surface tension (s) of the liquid as ν = r<sup>a</sup>ρ<sup>b</sup>s<sup>c</sup>. The values of a, b and c respectively are
steps: [ν] = T<sup>−1</sup>, [r] = L, [ρ] = ML<sup>−3</sup>, [s] = MT<sup>−2</sup>.
Mass: b + c = 0. Length: a − 3b = 0. Time: −2c = −1.
c = 1/2, b = −1/2, a = −3/2.

qs.stem: A body of mass 200 g is tied to a spring of spring constant 12.5 N m<sup>−1</sup>, while the other end of the spring is fixed at point O. If the body moves about O in a circular path on a smooth horizontal surface with constant angular speed 5 rad s<sup>−1</sup>, then the ratio of extension in the spring to its natural length will be:
steps: The spring force gives the centripetal force: kx = mω<sup>2</sup>(l + x).

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I: Acceleration due to earth’s gravity decreases as you go ‘up’ or ‘down’ from the earth’s surface.
Statement II: Acceleration due to earth’s gravity is the same at a height ‘h’ and a depth ‘d’ from the earth’s surface, if h = d.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
steps: g is maximum at the surface; it falls both above (g(1 − 2h/R)) and below (g(1 − d/R)): Statement I is correct.
Equal values need d = 2h, not h = d: Statement II is incorrect.
opts: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other as Reason R.
Assertion A: A pendulum clock when taken to Mount Everest becomes fast.
Reason R: The value of g (acceleration due to gravity) is less at Mount Everest than its value on the surface of the earth.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
steps: T = 2π√(l/g). On Everest g is smaller, so T is larger and the clock runs slow, not fast.
So A is false; R (g is less on Everest) is true.
opts: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct

qs.stem: If the distance of the earth from the Sun is 1.5 × 10<sup>6</sup> km, then the distance of an imaginary planet from the Sun, if its period of revolution is 2.83 years, is:
steps: Kepler’s third law: T<sup>2</sup> ∝ r<sup>3</sup>, so r = r<sub>E</sub> (T/1 yr)<sup>2/3</sup>.
2.83<sup>2</sup> ≈ 8, so r = r<sub>E</sub> × 8<sup>1/3</sup> = 2 × 1.5 × 10<sup>6</sup> = 3 × 10<sup>6</sup> km (taking the distance as printed).

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other as Reason R.
Assertion A: Steel is used in the construction of buildings and bridges.
Reason R: Steel is more elastic and its elastic limit is high.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
steps: Steel has a high Young’s modulus and a high elastic limit, which is why it is used for structures.
Both statements are true and R explains A.
opts: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct

qs.stem: Let γ<sub>1</sub> be the ratio of molar specific heat at constant pressure and molar specific heat at constant volume of a monoatomic gas and γ<sub>2</sub> be the similar ratio of a diatomic gas. Considering the diatomic gas molecule as a rigid rotator, the ratio γ<sub>1</sub>/γ<sub>2</sub> is:
steps: Monoatomic: γ<sub>1</sub> = 5/3. Rigid diatomic: γ<sub>2</sub> = 7/5.

qs.stem: The electric potential at the centre of two concentric half rings of radii R<sub>1</sub> and R<sub>2</sub>, having the same linear charge density λ, is
steps: A half ring of radius R and density λ has charge λπR, all at distance R from the centre.
Its potential is kλπR/R = λ/(4ε<sub>0</sub>), independent of R.
Two half rings: 2 × λ/(4ε<sub>0</sub>) = λ/(2ε<sub>0</sub>).

qs.stem: A cell of emf 90 V is connected across a series combination of two resistors each of 100 Ω resistance. A voltmeter of resistance 400 Ω is used to measure the potential difference across each resistor. The reading of the voltmeter will be:
steps: The voltmeter (400 Ω) in parallel with 100 Ω gives 80 Ω.
Total resistance 80 + 100 = 180 Ω, current 90/180 = 0.5 A.
Reading = 0.5 × 80 = 40 V.

qs.stem: A long solenoid is formed by winding 70 turns cm<sup>−1</sup>. If 2.0 A current flows, then the magnetic field produced inside the solenoid is ______. (μ<sub>0</sub> = 4π × 10<sup>−7</sup> T m A<sup>−1</sup>)
steps: n = 70 turns/cm = 7000 turns/m.
B = μ<sub>0</sub>nI = 4π × 10<sup>−7</sup> × 7000 × 2 = 1.76 × 10<sup>−2</sup> T = 176 × 10<sup>−4</sup> T (with π = 22/7).

qs.stem: The electric field and magnetic field components of an electromagnetic wave going through vacuum are described by E<sub>x</sub> = E<sub>0</sub> sin(kz − ωt) and B<sub>y</sub> = B<sub>0</sub> sin(kz − ωt). Then the correct relation between E<sub>0</sub> and B<sub>0</sub> is given by
steps: In vacuum E<sub>0</sub>/B<sub>0</sub> = c = ω/k.
So kE<sub>0</sub> = ωB<sub>0</sub>.

qs.stem: When a beam of white light is allowed to pass through a convex lens parallel to the principal axis, the different colours of light converge at different points on the principal axis after refraction. This is called:
steps: The refractive index (and so the focal length) depends on the colour. This defect is chromatic aberration.

qs.stem: An α particle, a proton and an electron have the same kinetic energy. Which one of the following is correct in the case of their de Broglie wavelengths?
steps: λ = h/√(2mK): for equal K, a larger mass gives a shorter wavelength.
m<sub>α</sub> > m<sub>p</sub> > m<sub>e</sub>, so λ<sub>α</sub> < λ<sub>p</sub> < λ<sub>e</sub>.

qs.stem: A photon is emitted in the transition from n = 4 to n = 1 level in a hydrogen atom. The corresponding wavelength for this transition is (given, h = 4 × 10<sup>−15</sup> eV s)
steps: λ = hc/E = (4 × 10<sup>−15</sup> × 3 × 10<sup>8</sup>)/12.75 = 9.41 × 10<sup>−8</sup> m = 94.1 nm.

qs.stem:
Match List I with List II.
List IList II
A. AM broadcastI. 88–108 MHz
B. FM broadcastII. 540–1600 kHz
C. TelevisionIII. 3.7–4.2 GHz
D. Satellite communicationIV. 54 MHz–590 MHz
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: AM broadcast: 540–1600 kHz (II). FM broadcast: 88–108 MHz (I).
Television: 54–590 MHz (IV). Satellite communication: 3.7–4.2 GHz (III).

qs.stem: A body of mass 1 kg begins to move under the action of a time-dependent force F = (tî + 3t2ĵ) N, where î and ĵ are the unit vectors along the x and y axes. The power developed by the above force at the time t = 2 s will be ______ W.
steps: With m = 1 kg, a = F, so v = (t<sup>2</sup>/2) î + t<sup>3</sup> ĵ.
At t = 2 s: v = (2, 8) m/s and F = (2, 12) N.
P = F·v = 4 + 96 = 100 W.

qs.stem: A uniform solid cylinder with radius R and length L has moment of inertia I<sub>1</sub> about the axis of the cylinder. A concentric solid cylinder of radius R′ = R/2 and length L′ = L/2 is carved out of the original cylinder. If I<sub>2</sub> is the moment of inertia of the carved-out portion of the cylinder about the same axis, then I<sub>1</sub>/I<sub>2</sub> = ______.
steps: I<sub>1</sub> = ½MR<sup>2</sup>. The carved part has mass M(1/2)<sup>2</sup>(1/2) = M/8.
I<sub>2</sub> = ½(M/8)(R/2)<sup>2</sup> = MR<sup>2</sup>/64.
I<sub>1</sub>/I<sub>2</sub> = 32.

qs.stem: A spherical ball of radius 1 mm and density 10.5 g cc<sup>−1</sup> is dropped in glycerine of coefficient of viscosity 9.8 poise and density 1.5 g cc<sup>−1</sup>. The viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity is 3696 × 10<sup>−x</sup> N. The value of x is ______. (Given g = 9.8 m s<sup>−2</sup> and π = 22/7)
steps: At constant velocity the viscous force equals the weight minus the buoyant force: (4/3)πr<sup>3</sup>(ρ − σ)g.

qs.stem: A mass m attached to the free end of a spring executes SHM with a period of 1 s. If the mass is increased by 3 kg, the period of oscillation increases by one second. The value of mass m is ______ kg.
steps: T = 2π√(m/k), so T<sup>2</sup> ∝ m.

qs.stem: A parallel plate capacitor with air between the plates has a capacitance of 15 pF. The separation between the plates becomes twice and the space between them is filled with a medium of dielectric constant 3.5. Then the capacitance becomes x/4 pF. The value of x is ______.
steps: C = Kε<sub>0</sub>A/(2d) = (3.5/2) × 15 pF = 26.25 pF.

qs.stem: If a copper wire is stretched to increase its length by 20%, the percentage increase in the resistance of the wire is ______ %.
steps: The volume stays constant, so the area falls as the length rises: R ∝ l<sup>2</sup>.
(1.2)<sup>2</sup> = 1.44, an increase of 44%.

qs.stem: A single turn current loop in the shape of a right-angled triangle with sides 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm is carrying a current of 2 A. The loop is in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.75 T whose direction is parallel to the current in the 13 cm side of the loop. The magnitude of the magnetic force on the 5 cm side will be x/130 N. The value of x is ______.
steps: The 5 cm side makes an angle θ with the 13 cm side where sin θ = 12/13.
F = BIL sin θ = 0.75 × 2 × 0.05 × 12/13 = 9/130 N, so x = 9.

qs.stem: A convex lens of refractive index 1.5 and focal length 18 cm in air is immersed in water. The change in focal length of the lens will be ______ cm. (Given refractive index of water = 4/3)
steps: f is proportional to 1/(n<sub>lens</sub>/n<sub>medium</sub> − 1).
In air: 1/0.5 = 2 → 18 cm. In water: 1/(1.125 − 1) = 8 → f = 18 × 8/2 = 72 cm.
Change = 72 − 18 = 54 cm.

qs.stem: The energy released per fission of a nucleus of <sup>240</sup>X is 200 MeV. The energy released if all the atoms in 120 g of pure <sup>240</sup>X undergo fission is ______ × 10<sup>25</sup> MeV. (Given N<sub>A</sub> = 6 × 10<sup>23</sup>)
steps: 120 g of <sup>240</sup>X is 0.5 mol = 3 × 10<sup>23</sup> atoms.
Energy = 3 × 10<sup>23</sup> × 200 MeV = 6 × 10<sup>25</sup> MeV.

qs.stem: What is the number of unpaired electron(s) in the highest occupied molecular orbital of the following species: N<sub>2</sub>, N<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup>, O<sub>2</sub>, O<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup>?
steps: N<sub>2</sub>: all paired, 0. N<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup>: one electron removed from σ2p, 1.
O<sub>2</sub>: two unpaired electrons in π*, 2. O<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup>: one electron removed from π*, 1.

qs.stem: In which of the following reactions does hydrogen peroxide act as a reducing agent?
steps: A reducing agent is itself oxidised. Only in the third reaction is H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> oxidised (O: −1 to 0, giving O<sub>2</sub>).
In the others it is reduced to H<sub>2</sub>O or OH<sup>−</sup>.

qs.stem:
Identify the correct statements about alkali metals.
A. The order of standard reduction potential (M+|M) for alkali metal ions is Na > Rb > Li.
B. CsI is highly soluble in water.
C. Lithium carbonate is highly stable to heat.
D. Potassium dissolved in concentrated liquid ammonia is blue and paramagnetic.
E. All alkali metal hydrides are ionic solids.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
steps: E°(Li<sup>+</sup>/Li) = −3.04 V, Rb −2.98 V, Na −2.71 V, so Na > Rb > Li: A is correct.
CsI is sparingly soluble, Li<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> decomposes on heating, and concentrated K in liquid ammonia is bronze and diamagnetic, so B, C, D are wrong.
Alkali metal hydrides are ionic: E is correct.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other as Reason R.
Assertion A: Beryllium has a less negative value of reduction potential compared to the other alkaline earth metals.
Reason R: Beryllium has a large hydration energy due to the small size of Be2+ but a relatively large value of atomisation enthalpy.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
steps: Be has the least negative E° in the group.
The reason is exactly that its high atomisation enthalpy offsets its large hydration enthalpy, so R explains A.
opts: A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A

qs.stem: The number of s-electrons present in an ion with 55 protons in its unipositive state is
steps: The ion is Cs<sup>+</sup> with 54 electrons: [Xe] = 1s<sup>2</sup>2s<sup>2</sup>2p<sup>6</sup>3s<sup>2</sup>3p<sup>6</sup>3d<sup>10</sup>4s<sup>2</sup>4p<sup>6</sup>4d<sup>10</sup>5s<sup>2</sup>5p<sup>6</sup>.
s-electrons: 1s, 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s = 5 × 2 = 10.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other as Reason R.
Assertion A: Benzene is more stable than hypothetical cyclohexatriene.
Reason R: The delocalised π electron cloud is attracted more strongly by the nuclei of carbon atoms.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
steps: Benzene is stabilised by resonance (delocalisation) energy, so A is true.
The delocalised π cloud is held more strongly, which is the reason for the extra stability, so R is true and explains A.
opts: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

qs.stem:
A student has studied the decomposition of a gas AB3 at 25 °C. He obtained the following data:
p (mm Hg)50100200400
Relative t1/2 (s)4210.5
The order of the reaction is
steps: The half-life halves each time the pressure doubles: t<sub>1/2</sub> ∝ 1/p.
t<sub>1/2</sub> ∝ p<sup>1−n</sup>, so 1 − n = −1 and n = 2.

qs.stem: The metal which is extracted by oxidation and subsequent reduction from its ore is:
steps: In the cyanide process silver is first oxidised (dissolved as [Ag(CN)<sub>2</sub>]<sup>−</sup> in air) and then reduced with zinc.

qs.stem:
Which one amongst the following are good oxidising agents?
(a) Sm2+ (b) Ce2+ (c) Ce4+ (d) Tb4+
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
steps: Ce<sup>4+</sup> (4f<sup>0</sup>) and Tb<sup>4+</sup> (4f<sup>7</sup>) readily gain an electron to reach stable +3.
Sm<sup>2+</sup> and Ce<sup>2+</sup> are reducing agents.

qs.stem: Which of the following cannot be explained by crystal field theory?
steps: CFT treats ligands as point charges, so it cannot explain why ligands are ordered as they are in the spectrochemical series (that needs π-bonding / MO ideas).
opts: The order of the spectrochemical series
Magnetic properties of transition metal complexes

qs.stem: The hybridisation and magnetic behaviour of the cobalt ion in the [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3+</sup> complex, respectively, is
steps: Co<sup>3+</sup> is d<sup>6</sup>; NH<sub>3</sub> is a strong-field ligand, so the electrons pair up in t<sub>2g</sub>.
Two d orbitals are free for bonding: d<sup>2</sup>sp<sup>3</sup> (inner orbital), with no unpaired electron: diamagnetic.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I: Pure aniline and other arylamines are usually colourless.
Statement II: Arylamines get coloured on storage due to atmospheric reduction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
steps: Pure arylamines are colourless.
On storage they darken because of atmospheric oxidation, not reduction, so Statement II is incorrect.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

qs.stem: The correct statement is:
steps: By mass, a person breathes roughly 15 times more air than the food eaten in a day (about 15 kg of air against about 1 kg of food).
opts: An average human being consumes more food than air
An average human being consumes nearly 15 times more air than food
An average human being consumes an equal amount of food and air
An average human being consumes 100 times more air than food

qs.stem:
Match List I with List II.
List I (type)List II (name)
A. Antifertility drugI. Norethindrone
B. TranquilizerII. Meprobamate
C. AntihistamineIII. Seldane
D. AntibioticIV. Ampicillin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Norethindrone is an antifertility (oral contraceptive) drug; meprobamate a tranquilizer; Seldane (terfenadine) an antihistamine; ampicillin an antibiotic.
So A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

qs.stem: The sum of π-bonds present in peroxodisulphuric acid and pyrosulphuric acid is
steps: Peroxodisulphuric acid H<sub>2</sub>S<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8</sub> has 4 S=O bonds, so 4 π-bonds.
Pyrosulphuric acid H<sub>2</sub>S<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> also has 4 S=O bonds: 4 π-bonds. Total 8.

qs.stem: If the pK<sub>a</sub> of lactic acid is 5, then the pH of a 0.005 M calcium lactate solution at 25 °C is ______ × 10<sup>−1</sup> (nearest integer).
steps: Calcium lactate gives 0.01 M lactate, the anion of a weak acid.
pH = 7 + ½(pK<sub>a</sub> + log C) = 7 + ½(5 − 2) = 8.5.
8.5 = 85 × 10<sup>−1</sup>.

qs.stem: The total pressure observed by mixing two liquids A and B is 350 mm Hg when their mole fractions are 0.7 and 0.3 respectively. The total pressure becomes 410 mm Hg if the mole fractions are changed to 0.2 and 0.8 respectively for A and B. The vapour pressure of pure A is ______ mm Hg. (Nearest integer) Consider the liquids and solutions behave ideally.
steps: 0.7P<sub>A</sub> + 0.3P<sub>B</sub> = 350 and 0.2P<sub>A</sub> + 0.8P<sub>B</sub> = 410.
Solving: P<sub>B</sub> = 434 mm Hg and P<sub>A</sub> = (350 − 130.2)/0.7 = 314 mm Hg.

qs.stem: The number of units which are used to express the concentration of solutions from the following is ______. (Mass percent, Mole, Mole fraction, Molarity, ppm, Molality)
steps: Mass percent, mole fraction, molarity, ppm and molality express concentration.
A mole is a unit of amount of substance, not a concentration. Count = 5.

qs.stem:
The number of statement(s) which are characteristics of physisorption is ______.
A. It is highly specific in nature.
B. Enthalpy of adsorption is high.
C. It decreases with increase in temperature.
D. It results in a unimolecular layer.
E. No activation energy is needed.
steps: Physisorption is not specific, has low enthalpy of adsorption, and forms multilayers: A, B, D are false.
It decreases as temperature rises and needs no activation energy: C and E are true. Count = 2.

qs.stem: The total number of tripeptides possible by mixing valine and proline is ______.
steps: Each of the three positions can be valine or proline: 2<sup>3</sup> = 8.
